ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, point C is on $\odot O$, extend BC to point D such that DC=CB, extend DA to another intersection point E with $\odot O$, and connect AC, CE. If AB=13 and BC−AC=7, what is the length of CE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $AC=x$,\\
since $BC-AC=7$,\\
therefore $BC=x+7$,\\
in $\triangle ABC$, where $AB=13$,\\
thus $AB^2=AC^2+BC^2=13^2$, that is $x^2+(x+7)^2=13^2$,\\
hence $x_1=5$, $x_2=-12$ (discard),\\
therefore $AC=5$,\\
therefore $BC=CD=12$,\\
since $\angle D=\angle E$,\\
thus $CD=CE$,\\
therefore $CE=\boxed{12}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, AB is an oblique diameter passing through the center O of the circle, with A at the upper left and B at the lower right; C is on the lower-left side of the circumference. The line BC is extended leftward to D, so D, C, and B are collinear and C is in the middle; the line DA is further extended to intersect the circle at E, so D, A, and E are collinear, and E is above the circle. The figure also connects AC and CE. Then reason: Let AC=x, then from “BC-AC=7” we get BC=x+7. Because AB is a diameter, ∠ACB=90°, and in the right triangle ABC there is x^2+(x+7)^2=13^2. Solving gives x=5 or -12; discard the negative value, so AC=5, BC=12. Also because D, C, and B are collinear and DC=CB, CD=12. And AC⊥BC, while BC and DC are collinear, so AC⊥DB; C is the midpoint of DB, therefore A lies on the perpendicular bisector of DB, giving AD=AB. Thus △ADB is an isosceles triangle, ∠BDA=∠DBA. Since D, C, and B are collinear, and D, A, and E are collinear, ∠CDE=∠BDA; also because the four points A, C, B, and E are concyclic, ∠CED=∠CEA=∠CBA. Again from D, C, and B being collinear, it can be known that ∠DBA=∠CBA, so ∠CDE=∠CED, hence △DCE is an isosceles triangle, CD=CE. Therefore CE=CD=12.
